newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-NATAL DOMINATE DAY TWO AGAINST FREE STATE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NATAL DOMINATE DAY TWO AGAINST FREE STATE.

text.p: play against Free State with some accurate bowling followed by
solid top order batting in their Supersport Series cricket match
After dismissing the visitors for a meagre 160 in their
first innings reply, Natal reached 120 for two when rain brought
a premature end to play with 7.2 overs still scheduled to be
Natal had extended their overall lead to 242, with Derek
Crookes making a brisk 52 at number three and opening batsman
Mark Bruyns a solid 48 not out in almost as many overs.
Earlier Free State, overnight 16 for one, succumbed to a
mixture of tight Natal bowling and loose batting and were bowled
Seam bowler Tertius Bosch, obtaining a little swing in the
overcast and muggy conditions, returned tidy figures of 3-40
from 23 overs while off-spinner Pat Symcox took 3-34.
For Free State, the only batsman to impress was 19-year-old
Boeta Dippenaar who top-scored with a patient innings of 81.
Dippenaar, sixth in the competition's batting averages with
67 going into this match, batted with great composure to reach
his second Supersport Series 50 of the season from 159 balls
He went on to accumulate 10 boundaries in all and occupy the
crease for just over four hours before being stumped by Keith
Forde off a Symcox arm ball.
Dippenaar shared in the only two stands of any substance in
the Free State first innings reply. He put on 42 for the second
wicket before Deon Jordaan (20) was yorked by the seam of Keith
Storey and then 33 for the eighth wicket with Philip Radley
Natal first innings 282 (Dale Benkenstein 100, Neil Johnson
Free State first innings (16 for one)
